issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not provide the expected Farm class skeleton: instead it defines a class named AnimalFarm (mismatched class name) and contains malformed duplicated package/class declarations and nested braces. The problem statement and UML describe a class Farm with an animals List and methods (addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong), and the solution repository implements a correctly named Farm class. The template's incorrect class name and syntactic corruption will prevent students from creating/compiling the intended Farm class and will cause confusion about the expected class name and signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file with a correctly named Farm class skeleton that matches the UML and solution: package declaration only once, public class Farm, private List<Animal> animals; a no-arg constructor that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(); public getter and setter for animals; public void addAnimal(Animal a); public void feedAllAnimals(); and private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) plus public void singFarmSong(). Remove the duplicate/incorrect AnimalFarm class and nested package declaration so students can implement according to the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named 'Farm', but the template implementation defines a class named 'AnimalFarm' in Farm.java. This mismatch (file named Farm.java containing public class AnimalFarm) breaks the one-to-one mapping students should make between the described entity (Farm) and the provided template, and will confuse students when the Main code (and the exercise text) refers to 'Farm'.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template file to 'Farm' (public class Farm) so the class name matches the file Farm.java and the problem statement. Also remove any accidental extra package declarations or duplicated code in the template so Main and the tests can reference and instantiate Farm as described.
